citations.title: Python Exercise Guide
citations.text:
Exercise Set A: Variables and Control Flow
Exercise A1. Write a program that asks for a temperature in Celsius and prints it in Fahrenheit. The formula is F = C * 9 / 5 + 32. Expected result: 100 Celsius becomes 212.0 Fahrenheit.
Exercise A2. Print all even numbers from 1 to 20 using a for loop and the modulo operator. Hint: a number n is even when n % 2 == 0. A common mistake is writing range(1, 20), which stops at 19; use range(1, 21).
Exercise A3. Implement FizzBuzz for numbers 1 to 30. Print "Fizz" for multiples of 3, "Buzz" for multiples of 5 and "FizzBuzz" for multiples of both. The test for multiples of both must come first, otherwise the Fizz branch will catch the number 15 too early.

citations.title: Python Faq Style Addendum
citations.text:
Frequently Asked Questions
Which Python version does the course use? The course uses Python 3.12 in all examples and tests.
Which editor should I use? Any editor is allowed; VS Code is used in the demonstrations.
Is the statistics module allowed in assignments? Yes. statistics.variance(data) returns the sample variance, while statistics.pvariance(data) returns the population variance. In the same way statistics.stdev is the sample standard deviation and statistics.pstdev is the population standard deviation.
Where do I ask questions? Post them on the course forum; answers are usually given within two working days.
